title: Gender Differences in Healthcare Utilisation: Causal Evidence from Unexpected Adverse Health Shocks
abstract: arXiv:2509.01310v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Women live longer than men yet report worse health. One common reading of this male-female health-survival paradox is that women also engage more with healthcare. We challenge that reading with causal evidence from the plausibly random timing of first-time non-fatal heart attacks and strokes in Danish administrative data. After such a shock, men increase their statin use and their general-practitioner visits substantially more than women. We find no evidence that the gap reflects a lower willingness among women to seek or take up care: men and women fill the same number of prescriptions, but women receive lower doses per fill, and the gap widens across drug classes where physicians have more discretion over what to prescribe. This points to provider behaviour rather than patient demand. translated_title: 医疗利用中的性别差异：来自意外不良健康冲击的因果证据
translated_abstract: 摘要：女性比男性寿命更长，但报告的健康状况更差。对这种男女性健康-生存悖论的一种常见解读是，女性也更频繁地利用医疗服务。我们通过丹麦行政数据中首次非致命心脏病发作和中风发生时间的看似随机性，对这种解读提出了挑战性因果证据。在这种冲击之后，男性增加他汀类药物使用和全科医生就诊的次数显著多于女性。我们没有发现证据表明这种差距反映了女性寻求或接受护理的意愿较低：男性和女性填写相同数量的处方，但女性每次处方获得的剂量较低，且在医生对处方有更多自由裁量权的药物类别中，这种差距会扩大。这指向提供者行为而非患者需求。尽管接受了额外治疗，男性在死亡率、发病率或我们可测量的劳动力市场结果方面并不比女性更好。鉴于女性...
tldr: 本文利用丹麦行政数据中首次非致命心脏病发作或中风的随机时间，提供因果证据表明男性在健康冲击后增加医疗利用更多，且差距源于医生处方行为而非女性患者需求，但额外治疗未改善男性健康结果。
en_tdlr: This study uses plausibly random timing of first-time non-fatal heart attacks or strokes in Danish administrative data to provide causal evidence that men increase healthcare utilization more after health shocks, with the gap driven by provider prescribing behavior rather than female patient demand, yet additional treatment does not improve men's health outcomes.
